email.body1:
Alyssa, saw Apptega expanded its GRC platform with Policy Manager, now supporting 15,000-plus programs and hundreds of service providers.

That kind of footprint usually means more in-market accounts than the team can personally touch before reps can work them, and that is exactly where pipeline goes cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Apptega off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.subject2: three drafts for your top accounts
email.body2:
Alyssa, quick follow-up for Apptega.

With Policy Manager live, in-market accounts usually outpace the reps who can work them, and the follow-up touches that actually book meetings are the first thing to slip. That gap costs more pipeline than any list problem.

I had our AI SDR draft three personalized emails to three of Apptega's top targets. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through them and the sequencing?
email.body3:
Alyssa, last bit of proof for Apptega.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Apptega's reply rate likely compares to peer GRC-tech teams. Want to grab time so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Alyssa, I will stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Rolling out a new module keeps a team busy, and I get that timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your motion? I will tailor it to Apptega either way.
